name: Brand Studio
description: Brand Studio turns a website URL into a saved Brand DNA (name, tagline, tone, colors, logo) and gives you linked tools to make on-brand campaigns, edit campaign assets, generate branded product photos and animate them.
shortDescription: Paste any website URL - get your Brand DNA, on-brand campaigns, product photos and videos
fullDescription: Brand Studio (#/brand, 'Brand' in the Image group of the side menu) is a home page for five connected brand tools. You paste your website address and click Analyze; the app reads the site and builds a Brand DNA record saved in your browser. From the Brand DNA editor (#/brand-dna) you can review and edit the identity, then open Campaign Studio (#/campaign) to generate concepts and platform-specific creatives, the Asset Editor (#/asset-edit) to place and style the headline, body and CTA on a campaign asset, Photo Studio (#/photo-studio, also reachable as #/brand-photo-studio) to generate product photos from 30 presets, or Animate (#/animate) to bring branded assets to life. Only Brand Studio appears in the side menu; the sub-tools are reached from its Brand tools cards, from buttons on the Brand DNA page and from the asset cards in Campaign Studio. Brand data is stored locally in your browser.
bestFor: Marketers, founders, agencies and e-commerce sellers who want on-brand social, ad and product visuals generated from their own website without designing from scratch.
whenToUse: You want the app to learn your brand from your website URL.
You want campaign concepts (4 ideas) and creatives sized for Instagram, LinkedIn, Facebook, X, web banners, email headers and YouTube thumbnails.
You want batches of product photos in several settings and styles from one product image.
You want to place, restyle or reword the headline, body and CTA on a campaign creative.
You want to keep your brand name, tone, colors and key messages in one place.
whenToUseAnother: Use Product Shot Studio (#/commercial) for a quick single product image or a UGC-style ad video without brand analysis.
Use Image Studio (#/image) for free-form images from text.
Use Edit Studio (#/edit) to retouch or change an existing image.
Use Find My Brand (#/find-my-brand) if you are looking for brand discovery or naming help rather than analysing an existing site.
Use Website Builder (#/website-builder) to build a site rather than analyse one.
Use Animate Studio (#/animate) directly when you already have an image to animate.
Use Video Studio (#/video) or Cinema Studio (#/cinema) for full video production.
keyFeatures: Analyze: paste a website URL, get Brand DNA (name, industry, tagline, value proposition, tone, personality, audience, key messages, colors, fonts, logo, screenshot, imagery and layout style).
Brand DNA editor with editable fields, chip lists, a full color palette editor and Past campaigns, saved locally.
Campaign Studio: 6 goals, 4 AI concepts, 8 platforms, up to three platforms generated at once with per-platform status.
Asset Editor: Headline/Body/CTA blocks on the asset's picture with Text, Position, Size, Align, Color, Background and Font, plus Swap image, Clean background and Upload image.
Photo Studio: 30 presets in 6 categories, multi-select, 1k/2k/4k, optional Direct MuAPI mode with advanced controls.
Personalize button on the Brand DNA page (when a screenshot exists) and on photo results.

featureExplanations.explanation: A URL box (placeholder 'https://your-website.com') and an Analyze button (enabled once you type). While running the button reads 'Extracting...' and a loading overlay says 'Extracting brand DNA...'. On success the Brand DNA is saved and the Brand DNA page opens. The app asks a backend to read the page (title, text, colors, fonts, logo candidates, screenshot), then uses AI to describe the brand from the text and, if a screenshot exists, the visuals.
featureExplanations.whyToUse: Starts everything; the other tools use this record.
featureExplanations.inputRequired: A website URL starting with http:// or https://.
featureExplanations.restrictions: Invalid input shows 'Please enter a valid website URL (e.g. https://example.com)'. An API key/sign-in dialog appears if no key is connected. If the page cannot be read, the AI guesses from the domain name (see limitations).

featureExplanations.explanation: Five cards under 'Brand tools': Brand DNA ('Review and edit your brand identity'), Campaigns ('Create on-brand campaigns'), Asset Editor ('Edit campaign assets'), Photo Studio ('Create branded photos') and Animate ('Animate branded creative assets').
featureExplanations.restrictions: Brand DNA and Campaigns open the brand you used last, otherwise your first saved brand; 'Brand not found' only appears when you have no saved brands. Asset Editor opens the most recent asset of that brand's campaigns. If the brand has no assets yet it shows 'Create a campaign first to edit its assets' and opens Campaign Studio; with no saved brand it shows 'Analyze a brand first, then create a campaign to edit its assets' and stays on Brand Studio.

featureExplanations.explanation: Up to six cards titled 'Recent Brands' showing brand name (or 'Untitled Brand') and industry (or 'No industry'). Clicking one opens its Brand DNA page.
featureExplanations.restrictions: Stored in your browser (up to 50 brands).

featureExplanations.explanation: Shows brand name and industry, website screenshot and logo, then editable fields: Brand Name, Industry, Tagline, Value Proposition, Target Audience, Imagery Style, Layout Style and Logo URL; chip editors for Tone of Voice, Brand Personality, Key Messages and Detected Fonts (type then Add or press Enter; click × to remove); and a Colors section with Primary and Secondary palettes. Header buttons: New campaign, Photo Studio, Animate and Save (shows 'Saved!' for a moment). When the brand has campaigns, 'Past campaigns' lists them by goal (for example 'Product Launch').
featureExplanations.whyToUse: Correct anything the AI got wrong before generating assets.
featureExplanations.restrictions: Edits are not saved until you click Save. Every color swatch can be changed with its picker, removed with × or added with +. The website screenshot is shown but cannot be changed. A Personalize button appears only when the brand has a screenshot.

featureExplanations.explanation: Pick a Campaign Goal (Product Launch, Lead Generation, Brand Awareness, Engagement, Thought Leadership, Direct Sales), optionally type 'Optional direction or theme...', then click Generate Concepts to get 4 on-brand concepts each with title, key message, CTA and Tone Notes. The goal cards stay visible, so you can switch goals before generating again. Click Select on one, choose platform chips (Instagram Feed, Instagram Story, LinkedIn, Facebook Ad, X / Twitter, Web Banner, Email Header, YouTube Thumbnail) and click Generate Assets. Up to three platforms run at once and each row shows running, done or error. Each asset card shows the picture, platform, format, headline, body and CTA, with Edit and Animate buttons.
featureExplanations.whyToUse: Fast multi-platform campaign creatives with matching copy.
featureExplanations.inputRequired: A goal; a selected concept; at least one platform.
featureExplanations.restrictions: Copy is trimmed to per-platform word limits (for example Instagram Feed: headline 8, body 30, CTA 3 words). Pictures follow the platform's aspect ratio (1:1, 9:16 or 16:9), contain no text (the copy is laid over them in the Asset Editor) and use your brand logo as a reference when it is a PNG, JPG or WebP image. Generating concepts again for the same goal updates one campaign; a different goal starts a new one. 'Back to Brand' returns to the Brand DNA page.

featureExplanations.explanation: Opens one campaign asset (from an asset's Edit button, or the Asset Editor card for your brand's latest asset). The canvas shows the picture in the asset's platform shape with the Headline, Body and CTA on top. Pick a block with the Headline / Body / CTA tabs or by clicking it, then change its Text, Position (3 x 3 grid), Size (small, medium, large, huge), Align, Color, Background and Font (your brand fonts plus system fonts). The top bar has '← Back to campaign', Swap image and Clean background (new AI picture, with or without the headline drawn in), Upload image, 'Animate →', a status message and Save (toast 'Asset saved').
featureExplanations.whyToUse: Finish a campaign creative: place the copy where the picture has space and keep it on-brand.
featureExplanations.restrictions: Changes are kept only when you click Save; there is no undo and no download/export. Swap image and Clean background need the asset's campaign concept. Opening #/asset-edit without an asset shows 'Asset not found'.

featureExplanations.explanation: Upload a product image (images only), optionally choose a brand from a dropdown (first option: No brand logo), type an optional Direction ('Describe the look, mood, or specific details...'), pick Resolution (1k, 2k default, 4k), then select presets in six categories: General, Beauty, Fashion, Food & Beverage, Home & Living and Tech & Hardware, five styles each (for example Studio white, Marble clean, Urban street, Restaurant plated, Scandi living, Dark techy). Each preset button shows its aspect ratio (1:1, 4:5 or 16:9); 'Select all' picks a whole category and 'Clear' undoes it. Generate Product Photos makes one image per selected preset, two at a time. Each result shows Download, Personalize and 'Animate →'.
featureExplanations.whyToUse: Many product visuals from one photo.
featureExplanations.inputRequired: A product image plus at least one preset.
featureExplanations.restrictions: Toasts: 'Please upload a product image first', 'Please select at least one photo style', 'Generated N photos', 'N photo(s) failed'. The brand dropdown controls which logo and colors are used and which brand the photo is saved under; choosing 'No brand logo' uses no logo. Each result's 'Animate →' button sends that photo to Animate Studio.

featureExplanations.feature: Photo Studio: Generation Mode (Brand API / Direct MuAPI)
featureExplanations.explanation: A toggle button labelled Brand API (default) or Direct MuAPI. Brand API uses the brand photo recipe with the Nano Banana 2 edit model, your product image and your brand logo. Direct MuAPI shows 'MuAPI Model (I2I)' (a list of image-edit models) and advanced fields: Negative Prompt, Seed, Steps, Guidance Scale, Denoise Strength, CFG Scale, Style, Strength and Prompt Extend.
featureExplanations.whyToUse: Power users who want a specific model or tuning.
featureExplanations.inputRequired: Choose a model in Direct mode.
featureExplanations.restrictions: If Direct MuAPI is on but no model is selected the studio falls back to the Brand API route. In Direct mode the text sent is your Direction only (the preset wording is not added), so every selected preset makes an image from the same text.

howToUse: 1. Open Brand Studio from the side menu (#/brand). 2. Type your website address into the box (placeholder 'https://your-website.com') and click Analyze. 3. Wait for 'Extracting brand DNA...'; the Brand DNA page opens. 4. Review the fields, fix anything wrong, then click Save. 5. Click New campaign, pick a Campaign Goal, optionally add a direction, click Generate Concepts, click Select on a concept, choose platform chips and click Generate Assets. 6. Click Edit on an asset to place and style its text in the Asset Editor, then click Save. 7. Click Photo Studio, upload a product image, pick Resolution and one or more presets, then click Generate Product Photos. 8. Use Download on results or Animate to bring them to life.
howToSteps: Open #/brand and paste your website URL.
Click Analyze and wait for the Brand DNA page.
Use New campaign for concepts and platform assets.
Use an asset's Edit button (or the Asset Editor card) to style its text.
Use Photo Studio for product photos.
gettingStarted: Use a public website address that starts with http:// or https://.
Sign in and connect your API key (a dialog appears otherwise).
Check the analysed Brand DNA and click Save before moving on.
requiredInputs: Campaign Goal + selected concept + at least one platform (Campaigns)
Product image + at least one preset (Photo Studio)
optionalInputs: Direct MuAPI model and advanced fields
Asset Editor text and style controls

inputDetails.name: Website URL
inputDetails.description: Address of the site to analyse.

inputDetails.name: Campaign Goal
inputDetails.restrictions: Choosing a goal card opens the Concepts step; the goal can be changed afterwards (a different goal starts a new campaign).

inputDetails.name: Platforms
inputDetails.restrictions: Selecting a different concept resets the platform choices.

inputDetails.name: Upload image (Asset Editor)
inputDetails.description: Your own picture behind an asset's text.
inputDetails.restrictions: Images only. If hosting fails the editor keeps a local copy in the browser, so very large files may not save.

generationModes: Asset Editor layout (no AI) with Swap image / Clean background (AI)

modeExplanations.description: Photo Studio uses a preset brand-photo recipe on the Nano Banana 2 edit model with your product and logo.
You choose an image-edit model and tune its settings.
AI writes 4 concepts, then per-platform copy and an image.

modelCapabilities: Photo Studio (Brand API mode) uses 'nano-banana-2-edit' (catalog description: 'Nano Banana 2 image editing and guided transformation.') with your product image and brand logo as references, at 1k/2k/4k, PNG output, in each preset's aspect ratio. Campaign Studio pictures, and the Asset Editor's Swap image / Clean background, use 'nano-banana-edit' with the brand logo as a reference when the logo is a PNG, JPG or WebP image, otherwise 'nano-banana' text-to-image, in the platform's aspect ratio; no resolution is set. Brand analysis and campaign/copy writing use the app's text and vision calls, which default to the 'gpt-5-nano' model. Direct MuAPI mode lists the image-edit models in the app's image-to-image and video-to-video catalogs that accept multiple images and a prompt. No prices, speeds or quality rankings are given in the files read.
outputs: Per-platform campaign assets (picture + headline + body + CTA)
Asset layout edits saved with the asset
limitations: Brand data (brands, assets, photoshoots) lives in your browser's local storage; limits: 50 brands, 200 campaigns, 500 assets, 200 photoshoots, about 4MB total.
If the website cannot be read, the AI infers the brand from the domain name and may be wrong.
Campaign asset pictures contain no text; the copy is laid over them in the Asset Editor.
Only one concept is turned into assets per Generate Assets run.
Only Brand Studio is in the side menu; other tools are reached from within it.

limitationDetails.impact: Clearing site data or switching browser/device loses your brands.
limitationDetails.workaround: Re-run Analyze on your site; keep a note of edits.

limitationDetails.limitation: Analysis may be a guess when the site cannot be scraped
limitationDetails.impact: Colors, logo and text may be generic.
limitationDetails.workaround: Edit the Brand DNA fields and Save.

limitationDetails.impact: You cannot download the finished creative with its text from this tool.
limitationDetails.workaround: Screenshot the canvas. The picture alone can be sent to Animate, and campaign pictures are also saved to generation history (without text).

troubleshooting: Analyze button is greyed out: type a URL first.
'Please enter a valid website URL (e.g. https://example.com)': include http:// or https://.
A sign-in/key dialog appears on Analyze: connect your API key and click Analyze again.
Error text in red under the form after Analyze: the site could not be analysed; try the home page URL or retry.

'Brand not found' on Brand DNA or Campaign Studio: this only happens when you have no saved brand or the link is for a brand that was deleted. Click 'Back to Brand Studio', then run Analyze to create a brand, or pick one under Recent Brands.
Toast 'Create a campaign first to edit its assets' after clicking the Asset Editor card: the brand has no assets yet; Campaign Studio opens so you can make some.
Toast 'Analyze a brand first, then create a campaign to edit its assets': you have no saved brand; run Analyze first.
'Asset not found - Open an asset from a campaign to edit it.': open the Asset Editor from an asset's Edit button or the Asset Editor card.
Photo Studio toast 'Please upload a product image first': upload an image (video is not accepted).
Toast 'Please select at least one photo style': select at least one preset.
'N photo(s) failed' or 'N platform(s) failed': retry; failed items show an error card/row.
'Upload failed (...); using a local copy' in the Asset Editor: the picture is still used; click Save, or try a smaller file if it does not stick.

troubleshootingSteps.issue: Analysis returns generic or wrong brand info
steps: Open the Brand DNA page and correct each field.
If you have no brands yet, paste your website address and click Analyze to create one.
Otherwise pick the brand under Recent Brands, then open the tool from the Brand DNA page buttons.

troubleshootingSteps.issue: Campaign assets fail for some platforms
steps: Run Generate Assets again with only the failed platforms selected.

troubleshootingSteps.issue: Photo Studio makes too many images
steps: Remember each selected preset makes one image, and 'Select all' selects all five in a category.
Deselect extras (or click 'Clear') before clicking Generate Product Photos.

commonProblems.whyItHappens: Colors are extracted from the site and screenshot.
commonProblems.howToFix: On the Brand DNA page change any Primary or Secondary swatch, remove extras with × or add one with +, then click Save.

commonProblems.whyItHappens: No logo was found on the site, or it is an SVG, ICO or GIF file, which the image models cannot use.
commonProblems.howToFix: Put a PNG or JPG address in Logo URL on the Brand DNA page and click Save.

commonProblems.problem: Text is hard to read on an asset
commonProblems.whyItHappens: The copy is laid over the picture.
commonProblems.howToFix: In the Asset Editor give the block a Background color, change its Color, or click Clean background, then Save.

steps: Select a concept, choose Instagram Feed and LinkedIn.

steps: Under General select Studio white and Lifestyle natural; under Fashion select Golden hour (3 images).

Download the best, or click Animate →.

Edit the headline, body and CTA text.
Set Position, Size, Color and Background for each block.

steps: Select Email Header, Web Banner, Instagram Story.

faqs.question: Does Brand Studio need my website?
faqs.answer: Yes, to create a Brand DNA you paste a website URL. Photo Studio can be used with only a product image.

faqs.question: Where is my brand saved?
faqs.answer: In your browser's local storage on this device.

faqs.question: What goals can I choose for campaigns?
faqs.answer: Product Launch, Lead Generation, Brand Awareness, Engagement, Thought Leadership and Direct Sales.

faqs.question: Which platforms are supported?
faqs.answer: Instagram Feed, Instagram Story, LinkedIn, Facebook Ad, X / Twitter, Web Banner, Email Header, YouTube Thumbnail.

faqs.question: What sizes are photos?
faqs.answer: Each Photo Studio preset has its own shape (1:1, 4:5 or 16:9), at 1k, 2k (default) or 4k.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Photo Studio and brand-photo-studio?
faqs.answer: They open the same Photo Studio page.

faqs.question: Can I edit the AI-written brand info?
faqs.answer: Yes, on the Brand DNA page, then click Save.

faqs.question: What does the Asset Editor card open?
faqs.answer: The most recent asset of your current brand's campaigns. If the brand has no assets yet it opens Campaign Studio so you can make some.

glossary.Brand DNA: A saved profile of your brand: name, tone, colors, audience, messages and style.
glossary.Concept: A campaign idea with a title, key message, call to action and tone notes.
glossary.CTA: Call to action, such as 'Shop Now'.
glossary.Category (Photo Studio): One of six groups of presets, like Beauty or Tech & Hardware.
glossary.Style (Photo Studio): A preset inside a category, like Marble clean or Dark techy, each with its own aspect ratio.
glossary.Direct MuAPI: Photo Studio mode where you pick the model yourself.
glossary.Asset: A finished creative: picture plus headline, body and CTA, editable in the Asset Editor.

tips: Fix the Brand DNA before generating campaigns.
Start Photo Studio with one or two presets to save time.
bestPractices: Click Save after editing the Brand DNA.
Keep Key Messages short and specific.
Review every generated headline before publishing.

relatedStudioGuidance.whenToMove: You just want one product shot or a UGC ad.
relatedStudioGuidance.why: Product Shot Studio is a focused form.

relatedStudioGuidance.whenToMove: You want to animate a photo or creative.

notConfirmed: Whether the web-page scraping backend is available in every deployment; when it is not, the code falls back to inferring from the domain name.
Whether brand data syncs to a cloud account; the store mentions it can be extended but only local storage was confirmed.
The output shape in Photo Studio's Direct MuAPI mode: no aspect ratio is sent and result cards are labelled 1:1.
Credits/prices/speed for any generation are not in the files read.

verification.evidence: Read BrandStudio.js (tool cards; the Asset Editor card opens the latest asset or Campaign Studio), BrandDnaEditor.js (fields, chips, full palette editor, Past campaigns with goal labels), CampaignWizard.js and CampaignPage.js, AssetCanvasEditor.js, PhotoStudioPage.js, plus brandAnalyzer, brandStore, brandNavigation, campaignGenerator (CAMPAIGN_GOALS, renderImage), platforms, layout, imageRefs, photoStudio, router and the muapi text/vision/image/imageEdit/imageEdit2 calls. No brand entry in instructions.js or studioLandingPages.js.
